A1.justification: Both PDFs describe APM under the same title and authors. The main text, equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A–H are readable and support reliable matching despite additions and relocation.

before.justification: V1 reports original computational experiments on protein folding, inverse folding, complex generation, antibody and peptide design, and appendix binder-design experiments and analyses.

after.justification: V2 retains these original experiments and adds inverse-folding perplexity results and a statistical comparison of folding across 20 random seeds.

M1.justification: The three-module architecture, training objectives, two training phases, and sampling procedures are retained. Naming FAESM in Appendix B.4 documents the implementation of a FlashAttention-based protein language model already mentioned in v1 Appendix G.

E1.justification: Training sources, single- and multi-chain protein tasks, antibody and peptide benchmarks, additional chain-generation scenarios, and Appendix F binder targets remain unchanged. The new perplexity and seed-based evaluations reuse existing task coverage.

E2.justification: The comparator sets in corresponding experiments are retained, including the appendix comparisons. ESM3 already participates in folding evaluation; ProGen2-base is a new scoring model, not a competing design method, and CpSDE is only cited.

E3.justification: Section 4.2 adds perplexity computed by ProGen2-base to inverse-folding evaluation. Existing splits, preprocessing, model sizes, training budgets, and downstream evaluation procedures are retained; the new seed and uncertainty information is assessed under E5.

E4.justification: The all-atom ablation in Table 4, torsion-angle analysis, chain-count and chain-by-chain analyses, and antibody, peptide, and binder case studies are retained. The new folding repetitions add statistical estimation rather than a distinct ablation or robustness scenario.

E5.justification: New Appendix D.2 reports folding with 20 random seeds, means and standard deviations for APM and ESM3, and p < 0.05 for both RMSD and TM-score comparisons. V1 gives no folding seed count or corresponding uncertainty estimates. This focused addition does not establish an increase from a known earlier run count, and the statistical test is unspecified.

E6.justification: Table 1 revises ESM3/APM mean RMSD from 4.94/4.90 to 4.71/4.83 and mean TM-score from 0.87/0.86 to 0.83/0.86, reversing their relative mean rankings on both metrics. It adds perplexity results, including means of 8.64 for ESM3 and 8.74 for APM; new Table 7 supplies seed-based folding summaries. These are revised reported results, not evidence of an improved model. Other matched results are retained.

T1.justification: The mathematical formulations, losses, and sampling equations in the main text and appendices are unchanged in substance. Section 3.1 corrects a rotation index notation without changing the underlying definition or reasoning.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, contribution list, and discussion retain the same claims about native multi-chain modeling, efficient all-atom generation, folding and inverse folding, and strong antibody and peptide design performance.

C2.justification: The new Impact Statement speculates about adapting the method to small-molecule, material, and chip design, extending its stated potential applicability beyond proteins. Existing mechanism explanations, failure analyses, and limitations in Section 5 and the appendices are retained.

D1.justification: The abstract changes a promised code release to a reported release at the same repository. Appendix B.4 newly identifies FAESM and its FlashAttention implementation, and Section 4.2 identifies ProGen2-base as the perplexity evaluator. These improve access and implementation documentation without establishing a changed training procedure.

R1.justification: V2 adds CpSDE to peptide-design related work and adds references for ProGen2, FAESM, and FlashAttention. The broader positioning and extended related-work discussion remain unchanged; other bibliography edits concern style or metadata.

P1.justification: V2 adds short Impact Statement and Acknowledgements sections and a statistical-validation subsection, with limited explanatory and terminology edits. Affiliation and proceedings text are updated, while the main narrative and section organization remain substantially intact.

P2.justification: Table 1 gains a perplexity column and more compact formatting, and a new statistical-results Table 7 shifts subsequent table numbers. Figures 9 and 10 move from the experimental discussion to standalone appendix pages. All figure assets are retained, so these are limited display and placement changes.

improvement.justification: V2 modestly strengthens evaluation through sequence perplexity and a 20-seed folding comparison with dispersion estimates and metric-specific findings. FAESM identification and the reported code release improve reproducibility documentation. The gains are limited because the statistical test is unspecified and the central complex-design evidence and existing limitations remain unchanged.
